discoveries: Theme-cluster pair-contrast batching cleared a HEAD stage in one breath. The 7 remaining stage-2 blockers identified in 2026-05-22's log were exactly the 7 docs needed - the forecast held to the map. Pair-contrast structure for the closing batch: 1 single (sb_noise01) + 3 pairs (gl04/gl05, gm01/gm02, gm03/gm04). Singles work when they CLOSE an existing set (sb_noise01 closes rule-as-loom: rd, ls, ca already had pair-contrast; noise is the fourth, no remaining contrast partner needed). Pairs work when they CONTRAST a parameter axis (gl04 vs gl05 contrasts param-variation vs param-breakdown; gm01 vs gm02 contrasts constant vs varying radius; gm03 vs gm04 contrasts inside-cavity vs outside-obstacle). The cluster reading becomes a small theorem: each map names a position in a structured parameter space.

The gm-family (glass-meets-mould) cluster makes the integration-phase claim visible: form = body-physics + external-geometry. The gl-family already made the claim weaker (form = pin + gravity + body); the gm-family sharpens it by replacing pin+gravity with cavity-or-obstacle, which is a single object instead of two. gm03 (rounded-corner box) makes legible something gm01/gm02 hid - the cavity does not fully determine the vessel; the body's bending stiffness decides corner radius. So form is not 'cavity' alone but 'cavity x body-stiffness'. The corners are where the parameter shows itself.

gm04 (pressed onto sphere) inverts the topology: instead of body-in-cavity, form-in-body. This is the same body-physics, the same gravity, the same contact-projection - but the constraint geometry is OUTSIDE the body instead of INSIDE. The vessel that emerges (cloth draping over a sphere) shares the family signature with bottle-in-cylinder despite being topologically opposite. Crafts that match the gm-pattern (vacuum-forming, glass-slumping, draping in fashion, pottery on mandrel) similarly use either cavity OR master interchangeably - the same physical principle is at work and the simulation makes that principle explicit.

discoveries: THE CAP WAS THE VERDICT. build_dna_gallery trims a declared axis from the END of its value list until the cross product fits --max (default 9), and said nothing. dot_aligner declares opening(4) x workings(4) = 16; at the default cap it rendered 4 x 2, and artifact_dna_critic published `workings INERT, focus 2.27%`. Swept over all four values the same axis reads 2.07% frame / 37.49% focus and BITES. The entire signal was in `expression`, which the cap dropped — and the other dropped value was `operands`, the artifact's own default, i.e. the baseline the other values are supposed to differ FROM. This is the sixth entry in the harness-before-design log and the first where the harness's BUDGET, not its vocabulary (cctv, science_screen), its framing (random_walk) or its denominator (temporal_lint, render_lint), produced the false verdict. A dropped value is invisible downstream by construction: the manifest lists what rendered, so a truncated axis and a complete one are the same document. FIXED — the sweep now records `partial_axes` in the manifest and the critic prints [PARTIAL n/m values] on the row, because a caveat that is not on the table is not read.

discoveries: A BREATH'S BASELINE IS NOT ATOMIC, AND THIS ONE STRADDLED TWO COMMITS. The Baseline phase spends ~6 minutes in Godot (release gate F alone is a ~70 s headless walk, run up to 3 times). During this breath's baseline (09:04-09:11) an interactive session was editing commons/scenes/endless_museum.gd, saved it at 09:11:29, and committed twice at 09:15. The tell was not git status - it was that a Grep and a Read of the SAME file minutes apart disagreed by 43 lines, while `git diff --stat` on that path printed NOTHING, because by the time I diffed it the other session had committed and the working tree matched the new HEAD again. So the file appeared clean at both ends and had changed in the middle. Every number in this breath's Baseline is therefore a measurement of a tree that no longer exists, and no single tree produced all of them. The standing rule was 'two git status reads are not enough'; the sharper form is that git status cannot see a change that has already been committed by someone else, and the only reliable witness was mtime.

A HYPOTHESIS ABOUT THE 44.65 STALL, GROUNDED IN THE LOG AND THE SEAL CONSTANT, HANDED OVER UNVERIFIED. discoveries: THE PROP DEALER WAS INNOCENT, AND THE INSTRUMENT THAT CLEARED IT TOOK ONE RUN. Three breaths ended with the same well-posed hypothesis - the bench placer guards its erasures and the prop dealer's occupies_floor erasure does not, so a floor prop dealt into a doorway would sever the walk map - and none could test it, because the walk map lives for 33 seconds inside a headless process and dies with it. Recording who erased each cell, and dumping the frontier's far side into the verdict as a CUT, answered it on the first walk: of the 13 cells the walker could not step into, 6 were erased by its own stall handler, 6 were never stamped by the builder, 1 was a bench. Zero props. The hypothesis was reasonable and wrong, and the reason it survived three breaths is that nobody could ask the question - not that the evidence was ambiguous.

THE SEAL WAS BUILDING THE ONE FAULT A PLANNER CANNOT ROUTE AROUND. _occupied_cells clamps an artifact's seal to MAX_SEAL_RADIUS=2 - five cells - with four silent maxi/mini calls. The clamp's case is real and still live in this corridor: laser_measure measures 51 cells deep off a far-flung MESH, and sealing that would close a chapter. But the clamp applied to COLLIDERS too, and there is no such thing as a decorative collider. Measured: two lab_room bodies, 9 cells across each, dealt at (13,46) and (5,48), sealed to 5x5. Their colliders met across the whole 15-cell corridor at z=45 and ten of those cells stayed in _walk_cells. The plan routed straight through them, physics refused, and the stall handler unlearned six cells one at a time until its budget ran out. An under-seal is worse than an over-seal: an over-seal makes the planner route around a thing that is not there, and an under-seal sends the walker into a wall.

AND THE CHECK THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT ANSWERED BY RUNNING OUT OF BUDGET. Sealing the lab_rooms honestly made the first repair FAIL EARLIER - z=43, cut reading seal:lab_room x6 - which is the correct verdict and a red gate: the rooms really do wall off the corridor, and _seal_cells is supposed to take an artifact back out when its seal would sever. It did not, because _reaches_all early-returns TRUE at seen.size() > SEAL_PROBE_CELLS, and that limit was 400 - smaller than one 15x34 segment, let alone a museum. The flood filled the near side, never touched the far one, exhausted its budget and reported no severance. A bounded probe whose bound is below the thing it probes does not return an optimistic answer, it returns no answer, and the code read no-answer as yes. 4000 lets it look. Gate F then passed at 102.0/102.0 with ZERO stalls and ZERO cells unlearned - not merely reachable, but a walk map that agrees with physics at every step of 102 metres.

THE REPAIR COST ALMOST NOTHING, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH CHECKING RATHER THAN ASSUMING. Sealing colliders whole and letting the severance check bite could plausibly have emptied the museums - every large artifact refused, a corridor of bare plinths. Measured on the second deal order: segments placed 13/14, 14/14 and 13/14 artifacts, plus 3, 8 and 10 plinths and 13, 14 and 13 props. At most one refusal per segment. The honest seal is affordable because the corridor is mostly wider than the bodies in it; only the 9 m rooms were ever lying.

FOUR CONSECUTIVE BREATHS READ frontier_z AS A DIAGNOSIS AND IT IS ONLY A COORDINATE. 08-13 called the stall a joining fault (the seams killed that), 08-14 blamed the seal radius against the court residents (right family, wrong object - the courts were not even in this build), 08-15 blamed the prop dealer, and each reading was defensible from the numbers in the verdict. What none of them could do was name a token, because the verdict carried no provenance. The general lesson is the corpus's own, in a new place: a confident verdict was a fact about the rig four times running, and the fix was never a better inference from the same fields - it was one more field.

Neither was wrong; they were reading different museums. endless_museum.gd stamps a segment's cell grid in _write_built (:3453) when the segment finishes, but in replay mode the dressing pass is not run there -- it is appended to _stamp_queue (:3319) and drained frames later from _process. _dress_fixtures (:6707) and _dress_props erase their cells after that stamp, so a replay segment's grid is the shell. THE SWEEP THAT FOUND THE DEBT WAS HALF WRONG, AND THE COMMIT REFUSING ITSELF IS WHAT CAUGHT IT. Four files came back 'on disk, UNTRACKED'. A commit message was written declaring them clone-broken artifacts, with a Godot compile check behind it -- and git add staged nothing, so the commit printed status instead. NTFS answers Path.exists() case-insensitively while git ls-files is case-exact, so every file renamed by case reads as present-and-untracked under its old spelling. Two hits (newtoncradle.gd, rockfactory.gd) were that and nothing else. A verification step whose failure mode is SILENCE would have shipped this; the one that saved it did so by producing the wrong output loudly.

AND THE HALF THAT WAS REAL WAS REAL FOR A WORSE REASON THAN THE SWEEP GAVE. gravitywell.tscn asks for res://.../gravitywell.gd; the index held GravityWell.gd. A case-only rename on disk, core.ignorecase on, git reporting the tree clean for months, Windows resolving either spelling so nothing local ever failed. On a case-sensitive filesystem -- Linux CI, and the Android/Quest export path this project ships through -- the scene loads and its script does not. Swept rather than spot-fixed: 3,380 tracked scenes, 2 disagreements, both in physicssimulation, 0 after. The corpus-wide sweep is what makes '2' a finding instead of an anecdote.

discoveries: MY OWN CHECKER CONVICTED SIX ARTIFACTS THE ENGINE LOADS, AND ONLY THE THIRD INSTRUMENT WAS RIGHT. Godot 4 resolves an ext_resource by uid:// first and falls back to the path, so every file moved after its uid was minted reads as a dangling reference to a path-only sweep. Measured on this corpus: 571 stale res:// paths that the engine resolves by uid, against 0 spine-reachable references that genuinely do not resolve. The first sweep said 6 broken with placements and file names attached -- the most credible-looking output of the three. A checker that RE-IMPLEMENTS a resolver inherits none of the real resolver's fallbacks, and its false positives arrive with full forensic detail. The structural version: 147 tools under tools/ name res://, 3 mention uid at all.

THE MORNING'S CASE SWEEP WAS ONE-DIRECTIONAL AND LEFT EXACTLY ONE SURVIVOR. It compared scene references against the git index and found 2, fixed both, re-read 0. Widening the same direction tonight -- 4,379 res:// references across 3,388 tracked scenes and resources, every ext_resource type rather than scripts only -- still reads 0, so the fix holds beyond the subset it was measured on. The direction nobody swept is index against DISK: git ls-files is case-exact, os.walk reports the real filename, and comparing them across 34,095 tracked files finds MassSpringDamper.gd in the index and massspringdamper.gd on disk. git status prints nothing. A sweep proves a claim about the pairs it compares; the morning's claim was 'scene references agree with the index', which is true, and was read as 'the case class is closed', which is not.

THE BAR IS THREE AND THE LEDGER HOLDS FIVE, IN THE SAME CLASS, AND TWO OF THEM ARE TODAY. 2026-06-11: the pipeline scorer matched tokens literally while GridInteractablesComponent followed delegate_to chains, and the fix was written as 'mirroring the runtime resolver'. 2026-08-24: long_museum.py re-derived hall geometry in Python and drifted, and the same breath recorded having measured a scorer cost by flipping one character in the scorer's own logic RATHER than reimplementing it -- the right move, named as such. 2026-08-26: ten hand-rolled spine loaders, one of them returning empty against a spine of 22, with the note that two agreeing denominators were 'luck doing the work of a contract'. 2026-08-29 morning: Path.exists() standing in for git ls-files, NTFS answering case-insensitively, two phantom findings and a commit that refused itself. Tonight: path-only standing in for uid-first. prop-040 closed the spine-loader instance. The class is not closed, and the cheap general remedy is prop-018 clause 1 aimed specifically at resolvers: before believing what a modelled resolver CONVICTS, run it on a subject the runtime demonstrably loads and require it to clear that one.

GATE G IS RIGHT ONE LEVEL DEEPER THAN IT CLAIMS, WHICH IS WORTH KNOWING BECAUSE IT WAS NOT DESIGNED TO BE. It proves every spine token resolves to a scene FILE and stops. Asking the next question -- does that scene's own ext_resource list resolve -- over all 804 tokens and 1,322 placements returns 0 genuinely unresolvable references. So the gate's guarantee happens to hold transitively today. It is not gated, nothing would notice if it stopped holding, and the six stale paths inside spine artifacts are one editor save away from being rewritten and one uid loss away from being real.

discoveries: THE VERDICT THE GAME SHOWS WAS 81 DAYS OLD AND SAID PASS, BECAUSE THE RUNNER ONLY WROTE ITS REPORT WHEN ASKED. tools/run_release_gates.py wrote doc/reports/RELEASE_GATES.{json,md} only under --json-out/--md-out, and no caller in this ledger has ever passed them -- not the breather's command line, not the one in CLAUDE.md. So the tracked report sat at 2026-06-10 carrying `overall_pass: true` over FOUR gates while the live run failed four of eleven. ProjectDashboardOverlay.gd reads exactly that file as res://doc/reports/RELEASE_GATES.json and renders it on KEY_P, with nothing on screen to say when it was taken. Seven gates have been added since June and the headset has never seen one of them. The report is written by default now and carries measured_at / measured_by / head / head_subject / tree counts, written atomically and parsed back before it replaces the old one; the overlay prints the stamp and the age in days.

AND THE STALE REPORT WAS ARMED, NOT MERELY WRONG: OPENING THE DASHBOARD WOULD HAVE SWITCHED OFF THE SEVEN NEWEST GATES. _sync_release_gate_toggles_with_report() erased every toggle ID the report did not mention, and _save_release_gate_toggles() writes the result back over the TRACKED doc/reports/RELEASE_GATES_TOGGLES.json -- the file run_release_gates.py reads for --gate-toggles. Report knows A-D, toggles hold A-K, so pressing P deletes E F G H I J K, and the next gate run prints 'Enabled gates: 4/4 passing / Overall: PASS' with four gates red. It had not yet fired: that file's whole git history is three human commits ADDING gates. THE OLD BEHAVIOUR WAS MEASURED, NOT ARGUED. commons/testing/probe_gate_report_stamp.gd takes --overlay=, so HEAD's build was dumped out of git and probed: 0 of 7 unknown toggles survived, against 7 of 7 on the fixed build. Two traps on the way -- a dumped copy that keeps its `class_name` HANGS the boot on a duplicate class-cache entry, and an unguarded call() to a method an older build lacks aborts the rest of the function on a SCRIPT ERROR, so the probe first reported '1 of 3 failed' when 2 of the 3 had never run.

ALL THREE OF GATE I'S LOST EDGES WERE THE INSTRUMENT, AND SO WERE SEVEN OF ITS TWELVE NEARS. Not one sentence had stopped being true. (1) forces/Vectors_Act4b_Oscillation: the book quotes 'T = 2pi*sqrt(L/g) ... mg sin theta' and intent.md line 5 says the same thing in Greek and radicals -- an ALPHABET, not drift. Measured across all 269 anchors, the quote side holds four non-ASCII characters in total while the anchored files hold pi, theta, lambda, phi, Delta, partial, minus, times, middot, squared, approx and arrows in the thousands: a model reading mathematics writes it out in Latin. (2) randomness/Random_Space: the quote is 'seed_value = 1 ... enable_animation = false', which is TWO readings joined by an ellipsis -- both halves sit on lines 13 and 18 of the file it names, and matched as one span it could never be found. (3) isosurfaces/ISO_ImplicitModeling was the one real book error: the anchor said metaball.gd where the line lives in metaball.gdshader, and 'dist = smin(dist, sphere_dist, blend_factor);' being shader syntax was the tell. LOST 3 -> 0, and gate J's three LOST citations cleared with it, exactly as the runner's own comment predicted they would.

A GATE THAT GOES GREEN THE MOMENT YOU WIDEN ITS COMPARISON IS THE SHAPE OF ONE THAT STOPPED CHECKING, SO THE NINE MOVED VERDICTS WERE READ ONE BY ONE. Every move was NEAR->HELD or LOST->HELD -- none landed on the soft verdict, which means each is now a literal substring match after transliteration, a STRICTER claim than the NEAR it replaced. Three were opened against the actual file lines: Change_Velocity's ellipsis spans lines 204 and 206, VFM_06_Springs differs only in -> versus the arrow glyph, Fractal_MengerSponge's ellipsis spans a comment block. The ellipsis rule is stricter than what it replaced -- EVERY fragment must be present, not most -- and tools/test_edge_gate.py proves it: one true half and one invented half reads LOST, in both orders. Ten checks, including a quote with the right shape and the wrong variable (LOST) and a check that union and intersection do not normalise onto one token. Wired into gate I as detector_selftest, the way test_want_gate.py is wired into K.

GATE H CAUGHT MY OWN TOOL BEFORE IT SHIPPED, WHICH IS YESTERDAY'S WIDENING EARNING ITSELF BACK IN ONE DAY. The post-repair run read 8/11 with H newly red: 'present_but_untracked: tools/test_edge_gate.py, unreachable_from_a_clone: 1'. The 08-29 breath extended H from tools a runner INVOKES to tools it merely NAMES; today it convicted a file a fresh clone would not have, one run after it was written and before the commit.

MY OWN STAMP SHIPPED MOJIBAKE ON ITS FIRST RUN. subprocess.run(text=True) without encoding= decodes git's output with the locale codec -- cp1252 here -- and the commit subject landed in the tracked report as 'a-e-"'. Caught by reading back the file that had just been written rather than the console it had just been printed to, which is the only reason it was caught at all.

discoveries: THE PATHFINDER PRINTS THE FAULT IN PLAIN ENGLISH AND THEN CALLS THE MAP OK. On Tutorial_Single it emits 'Rule 2 [WARN] Teleport at (2,18) -- no structure row at z=19 to catch player' and 'Rule 3 [WARN] Teleport at (2,18) is NOT reachable from spawn via walking', then prints '1 maps checked: 1 OK, 0 FAIL (0 issues)' and exits 0. A tutorial map whose only exit stands two rows past the end of the world. This is not the blind-instrument failure the project has catalogued -- the instrument SAW it, described it correctly, and weighted it at zero. The standing note says map_pathfinder has ONE error rule; the sharper form is that everything else it knows is printed at a severity no runner reads. 62 cells in 29 maps are in this condition and gates C and G are green over all of them, because gate G asks whether a token NAMES something and never whether the cell EXISTS.

A SHARED SENTENCE CAN BE A FALSE SENTENCE, AND THE ECHO IS THE ONLY THING THAT MAKES IT VISIBLE. Gate K flagged transformation_cube and rotating_cube for carrying one description between them. The interesting fact was not the duplication: the shared sentence, 'A mysterious rotating cube', is simply WRONG about transformation_cube, which runs TransformationTween.gd -- sin(t * 3.0) * 0.4 m, a vertical bob, no rotation anywhere in the file. A wrong description on a single artifact is invisible to every gate in the suite. It only surfaced because it had been copied onto a second work, where a duplicate-detector could reach it. Duplication is a symptom of drafting FROM a neighbour, and drafting from a neighbour is how a false claim travels.

SIX OF GATE K'S TEN WERE MINE TO FIX AND FOUR WERE NOT, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS LEGIBLE IN THE DATA. Every line the gate flagged carries a `by` field. The six marked `by: draft` were machine-copied from registry descriptions and could be settled against the code. The four marked `by: hand` / `by: claude` trace to doc/SPEAK.md, where Palle wrote 'everything is made of triangles' three separate times (lines 62, 64, 69) -- the duplication is IN THE HUMAN SOURCE, and no amount of reading GDScript decides which of two triangles his sentence belongs to. A gate that counts human echoes and machine echoes in one number will always be four short of green, and that residue is correct: it is a question, not a defect.

discoveries: THE VERDICT WAS TRUE OF FEWER THAN HALF THE CELLS IT CONVICTED, AND THE HALF DECIDES THE REPAIR. Yesterday's detector said of all 53 off-world cells that 'the tokens resolve, the gates are green, and nothing is there'. Read against the engine, GridUtilitiesComponent and GridInteractablesComponent both place with `for z in range(min(dimensions.z, layout.size()))` / `for x in range(min(dimensions.x, row.size()))`, and `dimensions` arrives from JsonMapLoader.get_dimensions(), which returns map_info.dimensions VERBATIM. The engine sizes the world by the DECLARED numbers; only the Python side (place_artifacts.grid_dims_from_map) resolves size from len(structure), and its own docstring says why -- 269 of 2789 maps declare a depth that is not len(structure). So two faults wear one name: UNREACHED (outside the declaration, never built) and UNFLOORED (inside it, built, standing over void). 23 of the 53 were the first, 30 the second. Vectors_6 and Vectors_1 carry the SAME authored cell -- an info board at (0,8) over a 7-wide structure row -- and Vectors_6 declares width 9 so its board floats outside the world while Vectors_1 declares 7 so its board does not exist. One authored mistake, two repairs, and the difference is not in the cell but in a number in map_info.

A DOT INSTEAD OF A COLON TOOK THE TITLE OFF NINETEEN MAPS AND NOTHING OBJECTED. `an` is the annotation cube -- info_board.tscn, the board that displays the map's own name and description. Nineteen maps in the Forces/Vectors family write it `an.-90`; the corpus writes `an:-90` 108 times. The parser splits on ':', so the type reads as the whole string 'an.-90', matches no registry key, and the board is skipped. Gate G was green over all nineteen because it asks whether a token NAMES something and a token that names nothing at a cell that does not exist is not a name it checks. Twelve of the nineteen also sat one column past the declared width, so the typo and the position hid each other: fixing only the spelling would have made Vectors_6's board BUILD, floating one column outside its own world -- a repair that makes the defect visible for the first time is not a repair.

THE PATHFINDER'S TELEPORTER RULES ARE A CONVENTION NO OTHER INSTRUMENT STATES. Rule 5 wants the teleport cell to be VOID (h=0) -- you step into it; rule 2 wants row z+1 to exist WITH floor to catch the player; rule 3 wants the cell reachable from spawn. Placing Tutorial_Single's exit on the obvious walkable cell satisfied 2 and 3 and broke 5; (13,7), a void cell with floor behind it, silenced all three. Nothing but the pathfinder's own WARN text records that a teleporter belongs on void, and it prints all of it at a severity that leaves the map 'OK, 0 issues, exit 0'.

A MAP THAT DECLARES A ZERO DIMENSION IS AN EMPTY WORLD THAT LOADS WITHOUT AN ERROR. JsonMapLoader.get_dimensions() defaults width and depth to 0 and range(min(0, ...)) is empty, so no structure, no utilities and no interactables are built. 33 maps are in that state carrying 877 authored cells; 32 have no `dimensions` key at all and are all generated (Walk_* 17, Hung_* 4, Family_* 2, MindMap_* 3, Series_*, DrawGate_Test), the 33rd is Forces_PropGallery with the map-builder's {height, width}. Not repaired: the engine-side fix is a fallback inside get_dimensions(), which is the grid path, so it was measured and asked at forum 260901-w7z00 instead of taken.

discoveries: THE FLAT LINE IS A CEILING, AND SEVEN BREATHS OF REAL WORK PROVE IT RATHER THAN CONTRADICT IT. global_avg has read 6.091 on every breath since 2026-08-26 -- eight entries, seven of them full cycles that each changed the corpus (23 off-world tokens moved, a typo repaired in 19 maps, a tutorial's only exit restored, four gates hardened, two case-renames fixed). The number cannot move because 21 of 22 spine sequences sit at stage 6, vr_testing, with every earlier stage OK, and stage 6 is satisfied only by a human walking the maps in a headset. A headless breath is structurally incapable of moving this metric. Continuing to report delta 0.0 as the headline is the instrument describing its own ceiling; the honest steering numbers are the measured corpus classes (off-world UNREACHED 23->0, UNFLOORED 30 open, zero-dimension maps 33 open, divergent-dimension maps 224 open).

THE CHECK FOR TONIGHT'S FINDING WAS ALREADY IN THE ENGINE, WRITTEN, CORRECT, AND WEIGHTLESS. Looking for the declared-vs-derived split in code rather than trusting the morning's account of it turned up JsonMapLoader.gd:181-191: the loader computes structure.size() != declared depth and max_row_width != declared width, appends 'Structure depth (%d) doesn't match declared depth (%d)' to validation.warnings, and leaves validation.valid TRUE. So on all 224 divergent maps the game itself detects the disagreement, says it in plain English, and then sizes the world from the declared number anyway. This was not in the morning log, which reported the divergence as something the Python side alone knew.

AND THE ENGINE DOES NOT AGREE WITH ITSELF, IN THE SAME FOLDER. JsonMapLoader.get_dimensions() returns the DECLARED numbers verbatim; UtilityDataTemplate.get_dimensions() (commons/grid/UtilityDataTemplate.gd:72-83) DERIVES {width, depth} from layout_data.size() and the widest row -- the Python side's convention, inside commons/grid. Two rival definitions of world size are live within the engine before the tools/ boundary is reached at all, which is why 25 separate tools each felt free to pick one.

A NUMBER QUOTED FROM YESTERDAY IS NOT A MEASUREMENT. The morning log cites 269 divergent maps; measuring the live corpus tonight gives 224 over 2791 maps. Not a contradiction -- 269 is place_artifacts.py's 2026-08-29 DEPTH-ONLY audit and 224 is tonight's width-or-depth count under a different resolver -- but the two are not interchangeable, and a proposal built on the borrowed figure would have been arguing from a denominator it never defined. Both numbers are now written down with the denominator attached.

The steering metric prop-003 has been arguing against for ten breaths is not merely insensitive; it is one-way sensitive, which is worse than flat: a day of real work and a day of damage are indistinguishable above the floor and identical below it.

THE HALLS ARE NOT UNDOCUMENTED. THEY ARE DOCUMENTED IN THE COMPOSED LAYER WITH NOTHING UNDERNEATH IT. 3d37b5b2f (14:13) folded five 13x12 boolean halls into three larger ones. The five it retired each carried blurb.md AND intent.md; the three it created carry final.md and map_data.json and nothing else -- and final.md is not thin, Boolean_Works is 2440 words. Two independent instruments -- the pipeline scorer's stage 2 and the composition tool's own source ratio -- return the same verdict from different directions. AND THE CONVENTION QUESTION WAS COUNTED, NOT ASSUMED. The tempting reading was that the project has moved from blurb+intent to final.md and the scorer never noticed. The three that stand alone are the three born today. Had the count come back the other way the right output would have been a scorer change; it came back this way, so the right output is prop-006's 11th evidence update and no code change at all.

discoveries: THE CLASS IS os.path.exists() WHERE THE CODE MEANT git ls-tree, AND IT IS NOT ABOUT PROSE. Seven finished essays -- 9,567 words, the whole of foundationscrisis but its centrepiece -- sat untracked for two days while FOUR instruments called the tree clean: the pipeline scorer asks blurb.exists() OR intent.exists() and never mentions final.md; the pre-commit coverage hook reported 179/179 maps doc 100.0%; final_tags.py --check read all 49 final.md INCLUDING the seven and found 0 stale tags, because to a check that calls exists() an untracked file is simply present; release gates A-K read the working tree. Gate H is the single place in the battery that ever asks git anything, and it asks about tools. Three consecutive breaths (09-03, 09-04, 09-05) found instances of this one at a time -- the same signature gate H was written for, and the same remedy. Gate L is the class on the prose side.

THE 09-04 DEFERRAL WAS A READING, NOT A MEASUREMENT, AND IT WAS FALSIFIABLE. The evening breath found the same seven and left them, reasoning 'another session is writing them'. A day later six had not been touched since 15:37 on the 3rd and the seventh since 08:50 on the 4th. mtime turns that judgement into a number in one command. A deferral whose stated reason nobody re-checks becomes permanent by default.

THE NEW GATE'S OWN FIRST RUN WAS WRONG, TWICE, AND BOTH ERRORS WERE ONLY VISIBLE BECAUSE ITS OUTPUT DISAGREED WITH A HAND COUNT. It reported 19 files / 13,344 words against my 9 / 10,116. (a) Path.exists() on Windows is CASE-INSENSITIVE while git is not, so commons/maps/Facade_Baroque/blurb.md resolved on disk -- to Facade_baroque/blurb.md -- and was absent from git under the name asked for: ten false convictions, all ten files committed. (b) The gate checked that a sequence file was TRACKED and then read its WORKING-TREE content, so two uncommitted spine-sequence edits made it call the ISO_RhizomeBody and PRIM_RhizomeWorld blurbs stranded when HEAD declares neither room. Had I trusted the first run I would have told someone to commit half of somebody else's unlanded change.

AND THE FALSE POSITIVE WAS SITTING ON A REAL BUG OF A DIFFERENT KIND. facade_assembly.json declares five rooms in a case the disk does not have. Windows finds them; a Linux clone and the Quest export do not have those rooms at all. True since the 2026-05-14 preset stamp, and invisible to every gate because every gate asks the filesystem. On Windows, exists() is wrong in TWO directions at once: it cannot see that a file is uncommitted, and it cannot see that a name is the wrong case.

I GOT THAT FIX BACKWARDS AND A THIRD INSTRUMENT CAUGHT IT WITHIN A MINUTE. I lowercased the sequence to match the folders; verify_sequence immediately reported five NEW errors -- lookup_name 'Facade_Baroque' should be 'Facade_baroque'. Each map's own map_info declares Title_Case, so two of three sources already agreed and the DIRECTORY was the dissenter. Reverted, renamed the folders instead: 6 errors -> 1, and the remaining one predates this. When N sources disagree about a name, count which way the majority points BEFORE editing the one you happened to open first.

A GATE THAT READS ZERO ON A GOOD DAY NEEDS ITS ERRORS PLANTED IN A SELFTEST, AND THIS ONE EARNED ITS FIXTURES RATHER THAN IMAGINING THEM. Both real mistakes are now cases in --selftest: a case-mismatched room must leave scope without being convicted, and an untracked essay in a declared room must be convicted. run_release_gates.py fails gate L if the selftest fails, the same shape gate I uses for edge_gate.

THE PIPELINE READ 6.091 FOR THE TWELFTH TIME IN THIRTEEN. 21 of 22 sequences sit at stage 6, vr_testing, which needs a human in a headset; the essays landed and moved nothing because stage 2 asks blurb OR intent and both already existed. The instruments that DID see today's work were gate L (7 unreachable -> 0, 9,567 words) and verify_sequence facade_assembly (6 errors -> 1). THE BREATHER ALMOST COMMITTED A 13,201-LINE REFORMAT OF ITS OWN LEDGER TONIGHT, AND THE THING THAT CAUGHT IT WAS A CLAUSE ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN. Appending one 100-line entry to breath_log.json produced a diff of 13,201 changed lines across the three ledgers, because the write used json.dump(indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) while every one of these files has been serialised at indent=2, pure ASCII, since it was created. Nothing would have failed: the JSON is valid, the content is correct, the size floor passed, and the commit would have buried a real 158-line append inside 9,738 insertions and 9,589 deletions -- unreviewable, and unmergeable against any concurrent writer touching the same file. CLAUDE.md warns about exactly this for the artifact registries ('One json.dumps() round-trip once reformatted 15,121 lines') and the warning is scoped to a corpus the breather rarely touches, while the files it rewrites EVERY DAY carry no such note. It was caught only because prop-012 clause 2 requires printing `git diff --cached --stat` before committing, and 13,201 does not look like 100. Fixed by re-dumping at indent=2 with ensure_ascii default; the staged diff is now 158 insertions, 9 deletions. The rule that belongs in the Harvest phase is one line: read the file's existing serialisation and match it -- indent and ensure_ascii -- and treat a diff an order of magnitude larger than the append as a failed write, not a successful one.

THE GENERAL SHAPE: prop-002's discipline is 'verify the BLOCKER before believing it', and it has three clusters and four occurrences behind it. A GATE THAT READS SOURCE FOR REFERENCES READS A COMMENT AS A REFERENCE, AND IT CONVICTED THIS BREATH TWICE IN TWENTY MINUTES. Gate H was widened from INVOKED to NAMED on 09-08 (prop-044 clause 1) so it can see an orphan a reachability walk cannot. The cost showed up immediately on the first new test file written after the widening: its synthetic fixtures used tools/a.py and tools/brand_new.py as throwaway path strings, gate H read them as four referenced tools absent from disk, and unreachable_from_a_clone went 0 -> 5. Fixed by moving the fixtures out of the tools/ namespace -- and the COMMENT written to explain that fix named tools/foo.py as its example, so gate H went 0 -> 1 again. Two cycles. The widening is right and I would not narrow it; the note that belongs somewhere a fixture author will see it is that inside tools/, a path in a string literal or a comment is a reference, so illustrative paths must live outside that namespace.

THE LEDGER-REFORMAT TRAP REPRODUCED WITHIN SIXTEEN HOURS OF BEING WRITTEN DOWN, ON A DIFFERENT FILE, BECAUSE THE DIAGNOSTIC I USED POINTS BOTH WAYS. Last night's rule: read the file's existing serialisation and match it, indent and ensure_ascii. I read it. I measured skill_evolution_proposals.json and found zero non-ASCII characters in 369,206 -- and concluded ensure_ascii=False was safe. It means the exact opposite: the file is pure ASCII BECAUSE it has always been dumped with ensure_ascii=True, and writing it with False unescaped 22 pre-existing \uXXXX sequences in other proposals, turning a two-object append into 35 insertions / 22 deletions. THE CORRECT TEST IS THE INVERSE OF THE OBVIOUS ONE: do not ask whether the file contains non-ASCII characters, ask whether it contains the two-character sequence backslash-u. Present means the file was written ensure_ascii=True and must stay that way. Caught only by `git diff --stat` before committing (prop-012 clause 2), which is now the third distinct write this year that clause has saved. A rule can be correctly consulted and applied backwards when the measurement that tests it is ambiguous, and this one is.

THE CRASH IS THE MILD FORM OF THIS CLASS, AND NOBODY HAS EVER LOOKED FOR THE SEVERE ONE. Both known victims announced themselves by throwing. The silent form is a comparison: the auto structure generator tests grid[nz][nx] == '1' and counts floor with cell == '1', both False against the integer 1, so on these ten maps a floor tile reads as void with nothing printed anywhere. Two years of this class produced two crashes and an unknown number of wrong answers, and the wrong answers are why the DATA was worth fixing rather than a third reader. A type fault that throws gets an hour of attention; the same fault behind an equality test gets none.

THE LEDGER-REFORMAT TRAP HAS A THIRD FORM, AND THE INVERSE TEST DOES NOT CATCH IT. The 09-09 rule: do not ask whether the file holds non-ASCII, ask whether it holds backslash-u; present means ensure_ascii=True. This file holds BOTH -- backslash-u escapes in some entries and raw double-encoded em dashes in others, from two different writers. So ensure_ascii=True rewrites the raw group and False rewrites the escaped group, and the first append measured 137 insertions against 79 deletions either way. A MIXED FILE HAS NO CORRECT ROUND TRIP. The append is now textual: insert the object before the array's closing bracket and assert that every pre-existing entry is byte-identical afterwards. Caught by git diff --stat before committing, which is the fourth distinct write this year that check has saved.

I measured it before writing a line, against gate L's live 164 rows. Explicit repo paths named in open threads: 2. Any mention of the room's name anywhere: 40 rows across 24 rooms. THE GENERAL SHAPE: prop-048 says verify a remedy before applying it because the corpus moves. This is the sharper case -- the corpus had not moved at all, and the prescription was still wrong, because it named a MECHANISM ('cross the paths') without ever measuring what that mechanism would match. A remedy that has not been run against the population it will judge is a guess with a commit message.

THE SAME DRIFT THE REMEDY WAS FIXING TURNED UP INSIDE THE REMEDY, WITHIN AN HOUR. Clause 2 adds --claims to forum.py so a heads-up carries its paths as data. forum.py has two writers -- it POSTs to /api/forum when npm is up and writes the store directly when it is not -- and the route builds its thread object field by field, so a claims key sent by the CLI would have been kept with the server down and silently dropped with it up. A claim filed during a working session would simply not exist, and the gate would go on printing the row anonymously while the writer believed they had said so. Both writers carry the field now, and forum.py reads the post back and prints what was lost if they ever disagree. This is the fifth time in the project's record that one rule with two implementations has cost a pass; the new thing is that it was caught by asking, before shipping, WHICH writer would handle the post.

A GATE THAT READS ANOTHER REPOSITORY MUST BE PROVED UNABLE TO CHANGE ITS OWN NUMBER. forum_claims reads ada_encyclopedia, which a clone of AdaResearch does not have, and the board changes hourly as sessions post. So the gate's verdict would otherwise depend on whether a companion checkout exists and on what somebody wrote an hour ago. The selftest now classifies, stamps the claims, and FAILS if the convicted set changed -- and the live battery reads the same 165 convictions, exit code and failing set with the forum present and absent. The reason to be strict about it is already in the record: gate N holds a 24-hour clock and went from 5 convictions to 21 overnight with nothing in the world changing. A verdict that took a hint from someone's post would be that fault in politer clothes.

discoveries: THE MEAN MOVED 0.416 IN FIFTEEN MINUTES WITH NO MAP CHANGED, AND THE CAUSE WAS THE READER'S PYTHON FLAG. The baseline read 6.083 and a re-run a quarter of an hour later read 5.667, with 8 sequences dropped to stage 5 and randomness at 7 of 14 validated. Nothing in commons/maps had moved; the only difference was that the second run was invoked as `python -X utf8`. The scorer spawns map_pathfinder.py with text=True, the child prints a cp1252 dash (byte 0x97), a strict UTF-8 decode kills subprocess's reader thread, stdout comes back None, `' 0 FAIL' in None` raises TypeError, and `except Exception: pass` records the map as unvalidated. Proven with a control rather than argued: HEAD's scorer under -X utf8 reads 5.667, the fixed scorer reads 6.083 under both modes. Fix: encoding='utf-8', errors='replace' and `or ''` -- the marker is ASCII so a lossy decode cannot move it. THE GENERAL SHAPE: a metric that swallows its own exceptions has an undeclared input, here the caller's PYTHONUTF8, and eleven consecutive readings of 6.083 agreed with each other partly because every breath invoked it the same way -- agreement between runs was never evidence that the input was declared. Worth knowing before anyone quotes a drop: any session that exports PYTHONUTF8=1 would have reported a regression of 0.416 and gone looking for it in the maps.
